source_title: Total Number and Ratio of GABAergic Neuron Types in the Mouse Lateral and Basal Amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Directly enumerates all major BLA GABAergic cell types with proportions: axo-axonic cells (5.5–6%), PV+ basket cells (17–20%), CCK+ basket cells (7–9%), SST+ dendrite-targeting cells (10–16%), NPY+ neurogliaform cells (14–15%), VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons (29–38%), and SST+/nNOS+ GABAergic projection neurons (5.5–8%).
summary: Stereological quantification in mouse LA and BA establishes that GABAergic neurons comprise 16% (LA) and 22% (BA) of total neurons. The major inhibitory subtypes and their proportions are: axo-axonic cells ~5.5–6%, PV+ basket cells ~17–20%, CCK+ basket cells ~7–9%, SST+ dendrite-targeting cells ~10–16%, NPY+ neurogliaform cells ~14–15%, VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons ~29–38%, and SST+/nNOS+ GABAergic projection neurons ~5.5–8%. This provides the first comprehensive census directly characterising all seven node types under study.
quotes: axo-axonic cells (5.5-6 %), basket cells expressing parvalbumin (17-20 %) or cholecystokinin (7-9 %), dendrite-targeting inhibitory cells expressing somatostatin (10-16 %), NPY-containing neurogliaform cells (14-15 %), VIP and/or calretinin-expressing interneuron-selective interneurons (29-38 %) and GABAergic projection neurons expressing somatostatin and neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS
the ratio of GABAergic neurons in the BA (22 %) is significantly higher than in the LA (16 %) in both male and female mice
